title: Smallest Divisors: f(n) = o(n) for Almost All n

problemStatement.formal: Let f(n) be the minimal m whose partial divisor sums include n. Is |{k ≤ n : f(k)/k ≥ ε}|/n → 0 for each ε > 0?
problemStatement.plain: Erdős asked whether f(n) = o(n) unconditionally (disproved by Tao) and whether this holds for almost all n (OPEN). The 'almost all' version asks: for each ε > 0, the set of n where f(n)/n ≥ ε has natural density 0. Key evidence: the sigma bound f(σ(m)) ≤ m shows f is small on the image of σ, and σ(m)/m is unbounded.
whyMatters: Part II of Erdős Problem 1054 — still open after Tao's disproof of Part I
Would show most integers have efficiently representable partial divisor sums
Connected to sigma function asymptotics (Gronwall's theorem, Mertens theorem)
The sigma bound f(σ(m)) ≤ m provides a direct approach via superabundant numbers

proven: f(σ(m)) ≤ m for all m ≥ 1 (sigma bound, Erdos1054OQ01.lean)
f(p+1) ≤ p for all primes p (prime structure, Erdos1054OQ01.lean)
There are infinitely many n with f(n) < n (from infinitely many primes)
axiomatized: tao_counterexample: f(n) = o(n) fails for all n (Tao's result)
mertens_sigma_primorial: σ(primorial k) / primorial k ~ e^γ log p_k → ∞ (Mertens theorem)
open: Main conjecture: HasDensity {n | f(n) ≥ ε * n} 0 for each ε > 0
Equivalently: limsup_N |{k ≤ N : f(k)/k ≥ ε}| / N = 0
Is limsup f(n)/n = ∞? (Part III of Erdős 1054)
